Government

Connecting public priorities with business possibilities.

Governments and public agencies can help create the conditions for business collaboration. SetuHashi can help connect priorities in Japan and India with relevant businesses, capabilities and opportunities, and support the work needed to develop them.

This includes national, state, prefectural and local bodies and public agencies, particularly economic-development and investment-promotion teams. Our involvement can focus on a region, an industry sector or a specific business initiative.

How we may work with government

  • As a client

    Commissioning a defined piece of work, such as an opportunity assessment for a region or sector.

  • As a participant or enabler

    Taking part in, or helping to enable, an initiative that businesses are developing.

  • As a supporter of collaboration

    Supporting regional and sector collaboration between Japanese and Indian businesses.

Where we can help

  • Develop opportunities for your region or sector

    Clarify regional strengths and priorities, and identify the sectors and business counterparts where collaboration could work.

  • Connect with businesses and investment prospects

    Identify relevant businesses and prospective investors, prepare the engagement and support the discussions that follow.

  • Help businesses navigate public-sector engagement

    Help an initiative work out which public bodies may be relevant, what they may need to see, and how to prepare.

The aim is better-targeted engagement, the right counterparts, clearer requirements and initiatives that are more workable in practice.

Public-sector engagement may matter, for example, for global capability centres (GCCs), water solutions or recycling. Requirements differ from one initiative to the next; not every initiative needs the same approvals, funding or support.

These are ways we could work with public bodies. They do not describe existing government assignments or imply privileged access, and we cannot guarantee approvals, funding, incentives or investment. Governments and businesses make their own decisions; qualified specialists handle applicable legal, regulatory and financial matters.
